summary.oneLiner: One of India's first professional-grade PCB manufacturers, now forward-integrating into Electronic Manufacturing Services (EMS) through its ioGems subsidiary.
summary.business: B C C Fuba India Limited manufactures professional-grade printed circuit boards (PCBs), originally set up in 1985 as a joint venture with Fuba Hans Kolbe & Co. (Germany) and DEG. Following its acquisition of ioGems Technologies Private Limited, the group has forward-integrated into Electronic Manufacturing Services (EMS), offering end-to-end solutions from raw PCB production to fully assembled boards for automotive electronics, e-mobility, telecom and consumer electronics customers.

risks.risk: The company itself discloses no risk register: Board's Report Section 35 states the SEBI provisions for a Risk Management Committee are not applicable and that the company 'does not identify any element of risk which may threaten the existence of the company'.
risks.note: There is no enumerated, company-identified risk list anywhere in the report - no MD&A Risks and Concerns section and no BRSR material-issues table - so investors get no management view of what could go wrong. Oversight rests on a Risk Management Policy reviewed by the Audit Committee rather than a dedicated risk committee.

risks.risk: Single-activity, single-site concentration in bare printed circuit boards, with the Board confirming no change in the nature of business during FY 2025-26.
risks.note: The whole earnings base sits on one professional-grade PCB facility established in 1985; the report names no second plant, no segment diversification and no geographic spread, so any disruption at that plant or a demand shift away from its board types hits all of revenue.

risks.risk: Execution and integration risk on the forward-integration acquisition of ioGems Technologies Private Limited, which takes the group out of PCB fabrication into Electronic Manufacturing Services (EMS).
risks.note: The MD&A calls this a significant step in a long-term strategic vision and the Board's Report records an investment of Rs 51,000 hundred (Rs 5.10 crore) in Iogems Technology Pvt. Ltd. EMS assembly is a different business model from a 40-year PCB base, and the report offers no ramp timeline, customer commitment or integration milestone against which the move can be tracked.

risks.risk: The growth narrative is anchored to government policy rather than company-specific contracted demand - the Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme expanded to Rs 40,000 crore in Union Budget 2026-27 and the USD 500 billion electronics manufacturing target for 2030-31.
risks.note: The MD&A's entire Industry Outlook rests on scheme money, import-substitution policy and national export targets. If incentives are re-scoped, delayed or captured by larger applicants, the demand tailwind the company is counting on weakens without anything in the report to replace it.

risks.risk: New domestic PCB capacity approved under the same policy push - copper-clad laminate facilities and advanced HDI PCB manufacturing units - is competing supply entering the company's own market.
risks.note: The MD&A cites these approvals as a positive for India's self-reliance, but they add capacity in the segment BCC Fuba sells into, and the report nowhere claims HDI capability of its own. The scheme that supports demand also funds better-capitalised entrants and the risk of price competition.

risks.risk: Working-capital and debt-service ratios weakened while revenue grew 54.4%, and the company flags both as significant (25% or more) changes in FY26 versus FY25.
risks.note: In the company's own Key Financial Ratios disclosure, trade payable turnover and debt service coverage each deteriorated by roughly 30%, and net capital turnover also fell, even as debt-equity improved. Faster growth funded partly by stretching payables is a structural cash-conversion watch item as the PCB and new EMS operations scale together.

risks.risk: Dependence on imported capital equipment and on foreign-origin process technology from the original German joint-venture partner.
risks.note: The facility was equipped with machinery from Germany, Italy, France, the UK and the USA and runs proprietary processes from Fuba Hans Kolbe & Co.; the Board's Report carries foreign exchange earnings and outgo under Section 134(3)(m). Equipment replacement, upgrades to next-generation technology and spares therefore carry import-cost and currency exposure, and technology refresh depends on external sources.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Increasing digitization of industries and proliferation of smart devices are driving demand for PCBs
- Emerging technologies in consumer electronics, automotive, healthcare and industrial automation are creating new opportunities
- India's PCB industry is entering a transformative phase supported by government policy initiatives (Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme) and global supply chain realignment toward self-reliance
- Growth opportunities across high-growth sectors such as automotive electronics, e-mobility, telecom, and consumer/industrial electronics
- The 'FUBA' brand continues to attract new customers while deepening relationships with existing clients, supporting demand

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Forward integration from PCB manufacturing into Electronic Manufacturing Services (EMS) through the acquisition of ioGems Technologies Private Limited, offering end-to-end solutions from raw PCB production to fully assembled boards
- Sustained focus on product excellence, customer satisfaction and cost efficiency to reinforce competitive position domestically and internationally
- Leveraging advanced manufacturing capabilities and proprietary technology to capitalize on digitization and smart-device driven demand for PCBs
- Continuous investment in employee training and skill development to align workforce capabilities with industry advancements, particularly in high-growth sectors such as e-mobility

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The company's principal expansion move in FY26 was forward integration into Electronic Manufacturing Services (EMS) through the acquisition of ioGems Technologies Private Limited, extending the value chain from raw PCB production to fully assembled boards. Separately, the company raised funds via a Rights Issue (allotment dated March 30, 2026) whose proceeds are intended for capital expenditure toward growth and expansion of the existing business; the Board later (April 29, 2026) approved changing this specific object to the purchase of plant, machinery and equipment. No proceeds had been utilised as of March 31, 2026.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- proprietary manufacturing processes and technology inherited from JV partner Fuba Hans Kolbe & Co., Europe's largest PCB manufacturer
- advanced machinery sourced from Germany, Italy, France, the UK and the USA
- established 'FUBA' brand that continues to attract new customers while deepening relationships with existing clients
- one of the first professional-grade PCB manufacturers in India, operating since 1985
- forward integration into EMS via ioGems acquisition creates an end-to-end value-chain offering (raw PCB to fully assembled boards)
